semantic_fixtures.covers: Exact face, costs, compiled program owners, emblem event and delayed return.
Up to two private discards, draw count, choice ownership and rejected excessive choices.
Empty hand auto-completes without a prompt or draw.
A discard redirected to the library still counts for the draw.
Required target, mandatory resolution sacrifice, and sacrifice replaced by exile.
Illegal target prevents the entire ability from resolving.
No sacrifice candidate produces no return.
Returned artifact's entry choice preserves the resolution.
A synthetic resultless Program continuation executes its tail exactly once.
Marker publication, separate counterable triggers, source departure and exact return.
Later zone changes cannot replace the captured graveyard incarnation.
Owner rather than former controller and event-time artifact type.
A token produces the trigger but cannot return.
Each stage is independently counterable.
A trigger created during an end step waits for a later end step.
Replacement-adjusted exile does not trigger the emblem.
Delayed return resumes after the returned card's copy choice.
Multiple emblems and simultaneous departures use APNAP and independent exact-object returns.
Emblem and pending work leave with their controller.
An emblem controlled by a surviving opponent remains when its creator's owner departs.
Accepted commands reproduce event batches and the final diagnostic snapshot.
The child scope is independent and unsupported trigger, identity, source and nested Program profiles are rejected.
The exact card can be declared as commander and is also admitted to a mainboard; their object identities are distinct.
